title: The process hunt
summary: The server's fans sound like a jet engine. Track down a CPU hog that keeps coming back, a backup that ignores you, a zombie and a process that needs to learn some manners.

ready.cmd: pgrep -f '[c]ookie-miner' && pgrep -f '[g]ary-backup' && pgrep -f '[o]ven-sim' && ps -eo stat= | grep -q '^Z'

tasks.title: Who is eating the CPU?
tasks.text: Something is burning CPU on `digestive`. Find the process using the most CPU and submit its **PID** (process ID number).
hints: `top -b -n 1 | head -15` prints one snapshot sorted by CPU. (Plain `top` is a live full-screen view: use it on a real terminal; the in-page terminal is line based.)
Or with `ps`: `ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head -5`. The PID is the second column of `ps aux`, the first column of `top`.

tasks.title: Kill it... for good
tasks.text: Stop `cookie-miner`. Then wait a few seconds and look again. Make sure it **stays** dead.

checks.fail_msg: cookie-miner is running (again?). Something keeps restarting it: who is its parent?

hints: `kill <PID>` asks a process to stop (signal TERM). `pkill -f cookie-miner` does it by name.
It comes back with a new PID? Then something restarts it. Every process has a parent: `ps -o pid,ppid,args -p <PID>` shows the **PPID**, then look up that parent with `ps -p <PPID> -o args`.
Kill the parent (`oven-watchdog`) first, then the miner: `pkill -f oven-watchdog; pkill -f cookie-miner`.

solution.note: On a real server the watchdog would be a systemd service (`Restart=always`) or a cron job, and the fix is to stop and disable that service. Killing the child alone is a game of whack-a-mole.

tasks.title: The backup that won't listen
tasks.text: `gary-backup` has been "backing up" for 412 days and has never written a byte. Stop it. (It is not going to go quietly.)
hints: Try the polite way first: `pkill -f gary-backup`. Still there? Look inside the script: `cat /usr/local/bin/gary-backup`.
`trap '' TERM` means "ignore the TERM signal". A program can ignore TERM, INT and HUP, but **not** KILL (signal 9).
`pkill -KILL -f gary-backup` (or `kill -9 <PID>`). KILL gives the program no chance to clean up, so it is the last resort, not the first.

tasks.title: There's a zombie in here
tasks.text: `ps` shows a process in state **Z**: a *zombie*. It has finished, but its parent never collected its exit status. Which process is the zombie's **parent**? Submit the parent's PID.
hints: `ps aux | grep defunct` or `ps -eo pid,ppid,stat,args` and look for `Z` in the STAT column.
The PPID column of the zombie's line is the answer.

tasks.title: Lay it to rest
tasks.text: You can't kill a zombie: it is already dead. Get rid of it anyway.

checks.fail_msg: There is still a zombie process (state Z).

hints: `kill -9` on the zombie's own PID does nothing. The problem is the parent that never calls wait().
Kill the **parent** (`crumb-collector`). The zombie is then adopted by PID 1 (the container's init), which collects it at once.

tasks.title: Manners for the oven
tasks.text: `oven-sim` must keep running, but it should give way to everything else. Give the running process a **nice value of 15** (without restarting it).

checks.fail_msg: oven-sim is not running any more! Restart the lab, or start it again: nohup nice -n 15 oven-sim &
oven-sim's nice value is not 15 yet (see the NI column of: ps -o pid,ni,args -p <PID>).

hints: Niceness goes from -20 (greedy) to 19 (very polite). `nice -n 15 cmd` *starts* a command with that value; `renice` changes a running one.
